proposal.summary: A bounds-checking bug in IOAccelCommandQueue2::processSegmentKernelCommand() leads to parsing up to 8 bytes out-of-bounds of the IOAccelKernelCommand header in shared memory. Command type 2 (kIOAccelKernelCommandCollectTimeStamp) writes timestamp data into that OOB area, allowing overwriting of the first 1-8 bytes of the subsequent page. PoC triggers on iOS 13 (iPod9,1 17B111).
proposal.affected_product: iOS 13 on iPod9,1 (17B111); macOS not tested but likely affected
proposal.cwe_quote: the check excludes the size of the 8-byte header, meaning that processSegmentKernelCommand() will parse up to 8 bytes of out-of-bounds data.

AV.quote: The attached POC should trigger the issue on iOS 13. Tested on iPod9,1 17B111.

PR.quote: The IOAccelKernelCommand is being parsed from shared memory, so the write is visible to userspace.

S.quote: The IOAccelKernelCommand is being parsed from shared memory, so the write is visible to userspace.

C.quote: This makes it possible to overwrite the first 1-8 bytes of the subsequent page of memory with timestamp data.

A.quote: This makes it possible to overwrite the first 1-8 bytes of the subsequent page of memory with timestamp data.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Reproduce the PoC on an affected device, confirm exact memory layout and whether the overwritten bytes can be leveraged for privilege escalation or information disclosure, and create a patch to include the 8-byte header in the size checks and audit other shared-memory parsing for similar double-fetch/out-of-bounds and non-volatile accesses.

evidence_quotes.claim: Bounds check excludes header allowing OOB parse
evidence_quotes.quote: the check excludes the size of the 8-byte header, meaning that processSegmentKernelCommand() will parse up to 8 bytes of out-of-bounds data.

evidence_quotes.claim: Command type 2 writes into OOB memory
evidence_quotes.quote: command type 2 corresponds to kIOAccelKernelCommandCollectTimeStamp, which actually *writes* into the OOB memory rather than just parsing data from it.

evidence_quotes.claim: Write is visible to userspace (shared memory)
evidence_quotes.quote: The IOAccelKernelCommand is being parsed from shared memory, so the write is visible to userspace.
This makes it possible to overwrite the first 1-8 bytes of the subsequent page of memory with timestamp data.
The attached POC should trigger the issue on iOS 13. Tested on iPod9,1 17B111.
AGXCommandQueue seems to do a poor job of treating shared memory as volatile, and I suspect that there are further issues here that are worth looking into.
